samples.first_diff: table_content: cell (1,2): expected 'The Budget restructures OCWS to concentrate its work on the systems that serve the most residents. Over the last decade, the Office has taken on a growing portfolio of small, overlapping grants that are costly to administer and difficult to evaluate. An internal review found that many awards were made without clear performance targets, and that a number of grantees could not show how funds had been used. The Budget proposes to consolidate these grants into three focus areas: drinking-water treatment upgrades, stormwater and flood resilience, and lead service line replacement. Each focus area would carry measurable outcomes and a public progress report. The Budget also ends funding for the Estuary Demonstration Program (-$212 million), which has not produced results that could be applied elsewhere, the Harbor Monitoring Pilot (-$88 million), the Regional Water Planning Councils (-$140 million), and the Small Systems Outreach Network (-$176 million). Technical assistance now delivered through these programs would be offered through the three focus areas instead, so that communities apply once rather than several times.
